identity.title: MUSE-ALMA haloes VII: survey science goals & design, data processing and final catalogues
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: Here, we present the overall survey science goals, target selection, observational strategy, data processing and source identification of the full sample.

Furthermore, we provide catalogues of magnitude measurements for all objects detected in VLT/MUSE, ALMA and HST broad-band images and associated spectroscopic redshifts derived from VLT/MUSE observations.

question.value: What are the physical properties of multi-phase circumgalactic medium (CGM) gas and associated galaxies in 19 quasar fields at z_abs < 0.85, and what are the magnitudes and spectroscopic redshifts of the full galaxy-selected sample across these fields?

evidence.quote: The MUSE-ALMA Haloes survey gathers a large multi-wavelength observational sample of absorption and emission data with the goal to significantly advance our understanding of the physical properties of such CGM gas.

Beyond the absorber-selected targets, we detect 3658 sources all fields combined, including 703 objects with spectroscopic redshifts. This galaxy-selected sample constitutes the main focus of the current paper.

analysis_steps.goal: Extract 1D optical spectra, classify sources, determine redshifts, and compile master catalogues

method.value: Extract 1D MUSE spectra using circular apertures (0.3-2.0 arcsec radius masked by PROFOUND segmentation map, optimising S/N at 5000-5200 Å for continuum sources; 0.5 arcsec radius for MUSELET emitters and HST priors), determine spectroscopic redshifts and confidence flags (1, 2, 3, 6) via template cross-correlation in MARZ (M. Fossati fork) plus visual inspection by two experts, and cross-match MUSE, HST, and ALMA coverage using TOPCAT.

evidence.quote: To obtain the optimal spectra for for redshift determination in each field, a range of circular apertures with sizes ranging from $0.3$ to $2.0$ arcsec in radius was used.
For the emitters detected by MUSELET and sources extracted using the broad-band HST images as a prior, a circular aperture of radius $0.5$ arcsec is used to obtain spectra.
To this end, we use the MARZ tool (cite: Hinton16) with the M. Fossati fork. This fork includes additional high-redshift templates and high-resolution templates well suited for VLT/MUSE data.

key_parameters.value: Circular aperture radius 0.3 to 2.0 arcsec (continuum sources, S/N optimised at 5000-5200 Å) or 0.5 arcsec (emitters and HST priors); redshift confidence flags 1, 2, 3, 6

evidence.quote: For each aperture radius, the signal-to-noise (S/N) of the spectrum at the wavelength interval spanning $\sim 5000 - 5200$ Å was calculated.

We therefore provide redshift confidences for each source. They are as follows: (1) spectra without emission or absorption features and no redshift estimate is possible, (2) a redshift measure is possible as the spectra contains low S/N emission and absorption lines, and (3) a robust redshift is determined where there is a high S/N emission line that is clearly resolved [OII] doublet or asymmetric Lyman-$\alpha$, one high S/N emission line with other fainter absorption or emission features, or with multiple clear emission and/or absorption lines, and finally (6) stellar objects.

claims.hypothesis: Combining VLT/MUSE IFS, multi-band HST imaging, and ALMA mm observations across 19 quasar fields with z_abs < 0.85 strong H I absorbers can simultaneously characterise the galaxy environment, continuum photometry, spectroscopic redshifts, and molecular gas coverage of both absorber-associated and galaxy-selected samples.
claims.experiment: Processed 19 VLT/MUSE cubes, HST multi-band images (with empirical quasar PSF subtraction), and ALMA cubes (PI, ALMACAL, and archival), performed continuum and emission-line source detection (PROFOUND, MUSELET, PHOTUTILS), and extracted 1D spectra for redshift classification via MARZ.
claims.result: Detected 3658 extragalactic sources across all 19 fields, obtained 703 spectroscopic redshifts (including 215 galaxies at z_gal < 1.2 below the quasar redshift), and achieved redshift completeness from 100% at r_mag = 20 to 60% at r_mag ~ 25.
claims.finding: The multi-facility observational campaign and processing pipeline meet the initial survey goals and provide a comprehensive matched catalogue to study the multi-phase CGM and cosmic baryon cycle.

claims.hypothesis: Constructing an empirical HST PSF from observations of other quasar fields in the same filter allows detection of faint galaxies at small angular separation from the bright background quasar.
claims.experiment: Masked objects other than the central quasars across all sample fields in the same filter, subtracted the sky, aligned diffraction spikes, scaled outer PSF wings, and subtracted the combined PSF from each target quasar.
claims.result: Diffraction spikes were robustly removed, revealing faint extended objects near the quasar centre that were previously hidden under the PSF.
claims.finding: Empirical cross-field PSF subtraction in HST imaging effectively uncovers faint absorber host galaxy candidates close to bright quasars.

evidence.loc: Subtraction of Quasar Point Spread Function
evidence.quote: For constructing the PSF in each filter for each quasar field, we used observations of all other quasar fields from our sample in that same filter, combining all such observations after masking objects other than the central quasars, subtracting the sky from each image, aligning the different images spatially so that the diffraction spikes overlap, and scaling them as needed in flux to make the flux levels match in the outer wings of the PSF.

evidence.loc: Subtraction of Quasar Point Spread Function

why_this_data.value: Absorbers selected with log N(H I) > 18 from HST UV spectroscopy and z_abs < 0.85 so that VLT/MUSE covers all optical emission lines up to [O III] 5007 Å, filling the redshift gap between COS-Halos (z ~ 0.25) and KBSS (z ~ 2), while HST resolves stellar continuum/morphology near the quasar and ALMA traces cold molecular gas via CO lines.

evidence.quote: MUSE-ALMA Haloes is based on a unique selection of known quasar absorbers based solely on two criteria: 1. measured H i column density log [N(H I)/cm$^{-2}$]$>$18, from HST UV spectroscopy, which delivers spectra with resolutions R=20,000-30,000 2. $z_{\rm abs} <0.85$, to ensure that all emission lines up to [OIII] $\lambda$ 5007Å will be covered by the VLT/MUSE observations

evidence.loc: Establish a Census of the Condensed CGM Baryons
evidence.quote: Our MUSE-ALMA Haloes dataset is optimised to fill the "redshift gap" between COS-Halos at $z_{\rm gal}\sim0.25$ and the KBSS at $z_{\rm gal}\sim2$, and thereby to probe the effects of cosmic evolution on the metal enrichment of the CGM at the peak epoch of star formation.

why_this_method.value: PROFOUND was chosen over SEXTRACTOR for VLT/MUSE continuum detection to avoid erroneous aperture blending in lower-resolution ground-based cubes; PCA sky subtraction was added to remove OH line residuals; empirical HST PSF subtraction from other quasar fields was chosen over theoretical PSF models based on past experience.

While objects in the HST images are typically separated due to the lower PSF FWHM, the blending of adjacent objects occurs in our VLT/MUSE fields.

Manual segmentation fixes with profoundSegimFix and visual inspection in MARZ and HST edge-artifact removal introduce subjective human steps that cannot be exactly automated.
